comments.body:
BRAINSTORM PROVENANCE (2026-09-04, /rebar-brainstorm). Recorded via the local CLI because the configured MCP server timed out on every call this session (open bug 9ea3-7d07-ea55-4496).

Operator decisions (in order): (1) all three seams MCP/CLI/library first-class; (2) notices are advisory + suppress only — no enforcement; scope = the notification system, mechanisms beyond notification are out (freeze, release/TTL, NOT-A-BUG registry → ideas burgundy-violet-narwhale, pure-dashing-sardine, aquarial-immoderate-schnauzer); (3) alerts file directly under the bug-creation contract, informed by this store's duplicate history — 24 canary-filed bugs, mostly serial duplicates from auto-close + re-fire (nine [binding-drift] in 14 days; two heartbeat bugs for a deliberately paused bridge) → eight anti-noise rules, recovery = comment never auto-close; (4) alert announcements go only to subscribed sessions, and runbook/guidance updates are in scope; (5) typed notice ticket type approved (schema impact enumerated on the notice child); design approved.

Research inputs (three reports + one critique, summarised in the child plans): server→client MCP push is dead on every target harness (Claude Code #7252/#36665/#45563 closed not-planned; Codex #15299/#17543/#18056 open; Cursor subscribe errors; OpenCode no resources) → boundary delivery (piggyback on tool results + hooks). Human trackers: auto-subscribe on assign + typed reason enum (GitHub Notifications API). Incident tools: curated-fingerprint dedup, firing→ack→resolved→regressed (Sentry), maintenance windows suppress notification not detection, 'the notice is the silence'. CI triage at scale (elastic-recheck, Treeherder, Sheriff-o-Matic): patchset-scoped vs trunk failures separated by where the job ran; poll-with-watermark is a legitimate topology; nobody auto-closes Actions-filed issues.

Critique corrections adopted: MCP delivery is an appended text content block only (no outputSchema change; verified mcp 1.29.0 accepts a CallToolResult from a tool fn); session hint sub-partitions inside the authenticated principal, never across; transport Mcp-Session-Id never used as durable identity; stale claims flag-only; ingester batches writes; feed carries no comment prose (prompt-injection boundary).

Execution order (depends_on recorded): diamond-miniscule-dassie → nephelite-sediment-apatosaur → {misleading-wizardly-yellowlegs, mysterious-zodiacal-fruitbat} → strained-lying-steed; aerobic-seraphic-blowfish after inbox + notice. Review in that order; the epic last.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Time-sensitive operational issues — `rebar-*` CloudWatch alarms and failures of scheduled/`main`-branch GitHub Actions workflows — are found today only by a human-launched sweep session (ledger `tomophobic-stilllife-mayfly`, `docs/user-guide.md` "Ops error-sweep ledger"). A session holding a ticket `in_progress` is never told when another session comments on, edits, closes, or takes over that ticket: `cross_session_warning` (`src/rebar/_commands/cross_session.py`) warns the *actor*, not the holder, and is silent over the MCP server because `claimed_session` is stamped from `resolve_session_id()` in the *server's* environment (`src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:71`). There is no project-wide, time-bound notice (outage, quiet window, maintenance) that every session sees.

Research (2025-26 OSS) fixed the shape: server→client MCP push is unsupported by every target harness (Claude Code #7252/#36665 closed not-planned; Codex #15299/#17543 open; Cursor subscribe errors), so delivery is at boundaries — piggybacked on tool responses (Kubernetes `Warning:` header, Slack `response_metadata.warnings`, git `advice`) plus harness hooks. Trackers auto-subscribe on assign with a typed `reason` (GitHub Notifications API). Incident tools dedup on a curated fingerprint and treat re-fire-after-close as `regressed` (Sentry). This store's own history demands that last rule: of 24 canary-filed bugs, most are serial duplicates from auto-close + re-fire (nine `[binding-drift]` tickets in 14 days).

## Approach

One shared **inbox delivery layer** — a per-session cursor, dedup, a hard byte cap, rendered on all three seams: an appended MCP text content block outside every tool's `outputSchema` (the registrar-proxy seam at `src/rebar/mcp_server.py:674-681`), CLI stderr lines with stdout and exit code untouched, and a library read API plus warning channel (`src/rebar/_lib_warn.py`). Three independent **read-time producers** feed it from the existing event log, so no broadcast queue and no per-delivery commit: (1) changes on tickets the session holds (auto-subscribed at claim) and on subscribed tags; (2) active advisory `notice` tickets — a new first-class type with typed `starts_at`/`ends_at`/`severity`/`suppress` carrying `session_log`'s carve-outs, expiry evaluated in the active-now query; (3) `ops-alert` bugs filed by a portable `rebar alerts ingest` operation under `docs/bug-creation-contract.md` plus eight anti-noise rules (dedup survives close for 14 days and reopens as regressed; recovery is a comment, never an auto-close; flap damping; N≥2 observations; `suppress` notices honored; storm grouping; per-run and per-day filing caps; ≤1 accumulation comment per 24h). Alert announcements reach only sessions subscribed to the tag; `claim` is the acknowledgement. Identity over MCP is the authenticated principal sub-partitioned by a client-supplied session hint, never across principals.

Positive rationale: boundary delivery is the only channel the harnesses honor; read-time producers reuse the event log rebar already syncs; a typed notice avoids parsing expiry out of prose (the GitLab stale-banner failure); the identity model keeps the existing auth trust boundary (`src/rebar/_mcp_auth.py:63` `PROXY_IDENTITY` ContextVar) intact. Scope is the notification system only: advisory notices, no enforcement, no claim TTL/release, no NOT-A-BUG registry — those are linked follow-on ideas.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A session that claimed a ticket over MCP or the CLI receives, at its next tracker interaction on any seam, one line per change another session made to that ticket (comment, edit, status change, claim lost, closed, link, tag) with a typed reason; proxy: the delivery child's cross-seam tests pass (CLI subprocess, library call, MCP in-process client).
- [ ] An operator can post a notice with a window; every session sees it once per session while active and never after `ends_at`; proxy: the notice child's read-time expiry tests and CLI/MCP/library round-trip tests pass.
- [ ] A new `rebar-*` alarm transition or allowlisted workflow failure becomes exactly one open `ops-alert` bug per fingerprint; a re-fire within 14 days of close reopens that same ticket; repeats add at most one comment per 24h; proxy: the ingester child's fixture-driven dedup/regression/flap/storm tests pass.
- [ ] Alert announcements are delivered only to sessions subscribed to `ops-alert`; an unsubscribed session gets no alert line; proxy: the subscription tests in the delivery child pass.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The scheduled ingester has run against the live CloudWatch and GitHub Actions sources without filing any duplicate: the operator records the run id, its report counts, and the timestamp as a ticket comment on the scheduling child.
- [ ] The runbook and agent guidance tell a monitoring or debugging session how to subscribe and how notices are posted; proxy: the documented commands exist and the docs-drift gate passes.

## Child decomposition

- **MCP session identity** — principal + session hint resolved on the server, `claimed_session` stamped over MCP, `cross_session_warning` live over MCP, client-config recipes. The foundation every other child consumes.
- **Inbox delivery + watched-ticket/subscription producer** — the `inbox` operation on three seams, cursors, caps, auto-subscribe on claim, `subscribe`/`unsubscribe`, `inbox.schema.json`. Delivers AC 1 and 4.
- **`notice` ticket type + `notice post/list/cancel` + active-notice producer + `suppress` field** — delivers AC 2.
- **Alert ingestion operation** — `rebar alerts ingest` with sources, fingerprinting, the anti-noise rules, ledger watermark, run report. Delivers AC 3.
- **Scheduled ingestion** — the GitHub Actions cron with a read-only AWS role and the live dry-run proof before codifying. Delivers AC 5.
- **Harness shims + runbooks/docs** — delivers AC 6.

Ordering: identity → inbox delivery → {notice, ingestion operation} → scheduled ingestion → shims/docs.
